title: POC weekly security sync - Elm Street Health
summary: Weekly POC security sync focused on SSO/SCIM, audit log retention and shipping, data retention/deletion during the pilot, and SOC 2 evidentiary requests. Agreed next steps include sending SOC 2 report, network diagram, and running an audit-log retention test. SE to validate KMS integration and log export to Splunk.
action_items: Priya (Redwood SE): run audit-log retention test against Elm Street test tenant and share sample export (due 2025-12-30)
Jordan (AE): send SOC 2 Type II report, network diagram, and DPA template (due 2025-12-26)
Marcus (CTO): confirm list of internal stakeholders for SOC2 evidence collection and schedule legal touchpoint (due 2026-01-05)
Liam (SRE): provide Splunk ingestion endpoint and log format requirements (due 2025-12-29)
Natasha (Head of Security): provide retention policy for PHI-related logs and desired deletion window during POC (due 2025-12-28)
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 artifacts and network diagram
SE to perform audit-log retention test and share logs
Customer to validate SCIM/SCIM mappings with Okta test tenant
Schedule follow-up pen-test scoping call (if required)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-12-23 14:00 UTC — duration ~57m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE); Priya (Redwood SE); Marcus Allen (CTO, Elm Street Health); Natasha Ruiz (Head of Security); Liam O'Connor (SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for jumping on, um, quick agenda — security follow-ups from last week, audit logs, SSO status, and SOC2 artifacts. toda — today we'll just run through updates.
[00:18] Marcus: yeah great, thanks. quick update from our side, Okta team's finishing the SCIM mapping, we ran into some attribute mapping quirks with groups and service accounts.
[00:29] Natasha: and from security i'm mainly looking at audit logs, retention and how we can ship them to our splunk instance, plus encryption key management questions during the pilot.
[00:40] Priya: okay great, we can cover that. quick note — we did the SAML flow with your staging okta tenant and we saw the login assertions come through, there was a small username attribute mismatch which Jordan flagged last week.
[00:54] Jordan: right, so status is SSO is functional in staging, SCIM pushes are mostly green, Marcus you mentioned groups — sometimes the group mapping requires a mapping rule on the Okta side to align with our role names.
[01:10] Marcus: yes, we'll share the mapping doc. question on sessions — is there session length or inactivity time we need to configure on Redwood Private? or is that controlled by our IdP?
[01:22] Priya: session lifetime is controlled by the IdP for SAML tokens; on Redwood side we respect the token expiry and we also have an idle session cutoff you can configure in the console, default 30 minutes. the Red wood private, sorry — Redwood Private console.
[01:39] Natasha: okay good. now audit logs — what's included by default? are admin actions, token usage, and syscalls included? and can we get raw events for SIEM ingestion?
[01:50] Priya: good q. default audit includes API calls (create/deploy/rollback), user auth events, role changes, and data-access events at a metadata level. we can provide raw event export for the POC — it's a JSON line format and we can stream or push via syslog to your splunk HTTP event collector.
[02:10] Liam: does that include chat completions or payloads? because PHI might appear in prompts and we need to know what's stored and for how long.
[02:20] Priya: by default we log metadata about requests (timestamp, model id, route, response time, request id) not full prompt contents unless you enable request payload logging for debugging. for the POC we recommended not enabling payload logging in prod; for debugging we can enable it on a per-session basis with redacted fields.
[02:40] Marcus: okay what's retention during pilot? we need a 90-day retention for audit logs but we might want auto deletion after pilot ends.
[02:49] Jordan: retention is configurable per-tenant. our default hosted retention is 365 but for Dedicated and Private you can set shorter windows. for the POC we can set a 90-day retention and set an auto-delete flag at pilot close — we'll make sure that's documented in the DPA.
[03:03] Natasha: can you demonstrate deletion? we want a deletion workflow and proof of deletion for later evidence.
[03:10] Priya: absolutely, SE can run a deletion job in staging and export the pre/post checks. i'll run that as part of the audit-log retention test.
[03:19] Jordan: great action there. next, encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)?
[03:26] Priya: yes, for Private and Dedicated we support CMK via AWS KMS and HSM integrations; for hosted tier we offer envelope encryption and we can integrate with your KMS via a key wrap pattern. there's sometimes a little config for key rotation windows.
[03:41] Marcus: for the POC we want Elm Street to hold the key if possible — is that allowed?
[03:47] Priya: on Dedicated yes, you can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) backed by your KMS. for the hosted environment we have a managed KMS but we can do a customer-stored key wrap with a gateway if needed — we'll need to scope network connectivity.
[03:59] Natasha: also need to see attestations — SOC two type two report, encryption algorithms, and any pen test reports.
[04:07] Jordan: we will share SOC 2 Type II report and network diagram after this call. i'll put that in a follow-up email.
[04:14] Marcus: perfect. legal/contract question — during the pilot can we have limited data residency, e.g., store logs only in eu-west for EU patients?
[04:24] Priya: yes, we can pin region for log storage and model execution on Redwood Dedicated / Private; hosted API may default to US regions but we have EU regions — for the POC we can provision eu-west if you need. there's a small lead time.
[04:38] Liam: re: SIEM ingestion, what format are logs and can you push via HTTP? we use Splunk HEC and prefer JSON(L).
[04:45] Priya: yep JSONL over HEC is supported, we'll need an HEC token and endpoint; we also support S3 export of raw logs if you want to pull them.
[04:55] Natasha: how about change history / audit for model rollouts — if someone flips a model variant for latency reasons we need an auditable trail.
[05:04] Priya: every config change is logged with before/after and user id, so that shows in the audit export. we also keep a model rollout history in the UI with timestamps.
[05:13] Jordan: any blockers on your side for next week?
[05:16] Marcus: we just need the SOC2, the network diagram, and for Priya to run that log retention test. also wants to confirm the Okta mapping.
[05:24] Natasha: a few clarifying q's — one, will Redwood redact PHI automatically from logs or is that manual? two, do you provide a DLP integration?
[05:33] Priya: we don't automatically redact PHI out of request payloads unless you enable redaction rules; we do offer a configurable redaction layer and can hook an on-prem DLP via webhook for real-time tagging. for logs we recommend keeping only metadata unless you need payloads for debugging.
[05:51] Marcus: earlier you mentioned prefix/KV cache — is there any risk of cached prompt tokens being stored in a shared cache?
[05:59] Priya: good catch — we use per-tenant KV caches and for Dedicated/Private there's full isolation. hosted tiers use multi-tenant caches but we isolate keys logically. for Elm Street POC we'll run on a dedicated pool to avoid any cross-tenant risk. (some background noise)
[06:20] Liam: can you provide sample audit log entries? schema? that'll speed up our Splunk mapping.
[06:26] Priya: yes i'll export sample JSONL and push via a secure transfer link; that'll include timestamp, user, action, resource, and optional request_id.
[06:36] Jordan: i'm going to recap actions after Priya's test.
[06:40] Marcus: also, on SOC2 evidence, we may ask for OS-level configs for the host if you're providing Dedicated — is that available?
[06:49] Priya: yes for Dedicated we can provide a limited set of host-level configs and a penetration test report under an NDA. for Private on-prem you'll manage the hosts.
[06:59] Natasha: can we run a short live demo of deletion? just see the job and how it's logged?
[07:05] Priya: we can do that in staging right now if you want, but maybe better to run the retention test and capture the demo video. would you prefer live?
[07:13] Marcus: a recorded demo is fine as long as the steps and logs are exported.
[07:18] Priya: noted. i'll capture pre/post logs.
[07:22] Jordan: any legal hold concerns if we auto-delete logs? some of our clinical logs need to be kept longer under subpoena.
[07:30] Natasha: yes we need a legal-hold capability. can Redwood exempt specific datasets from deletion?
[07:36] Priya: yes, we support legal-hold tags at the object level which prevent deletion until the hold is removed; we'll document the API for that.
[07:46] Marcus: great. next, penetration testing — timeline to approve redwood-run pen test?
[07:52] Priya: typical turnaround is 2-3 weeks to schedule and get scope approval; we'd run it under a signed scope and share the report under NDA.
[07:59] Liam: for the audit-log retention test, can you include some simulated PHI entries so we can validate redaction rules?
[08:06] Priya: yes we can seed synthetic PHI and show redaction working in the pipeline.
[08:12] Natasha: one more: SOC2 evidence — do you have the controls mapped to COBIT or NIST so our auditors can crosswalk?
[08:20] Jordan: we have a controls mapping doc that maps SOC2 controls to NIST 800-53 and ISO where feasible; i'll attach that with the SOC2 report.
[08:29] Marcus: ok thanks. any other open ques?
[08:33] Natasha: just timeline — we need these artifacts before our internal security review on Jan 6th.
[08:39] Jordan: we'll aim to get SOC2 + network diagram by Dec 26th and Priya's test results by Dec 30th.
[08:46] Marcus: that works. let's confirm next sync date.
[08:50] Jordan: propose Jan 2nd 14:00 UTC for a short follow-up; we'll send calendar invite.
[08:57] Marcus: yep fine.
[09:00] Jordan: quick recap of next steps: i'll send SOC2, DPA template, and network diagram; Priya runs audit-log retention test and exports sample JSONL for Splunk; Elm Street to provide HEC endpoint and retention policy.
[09:15] Natasha: thanks all.
[09:18] Jordan: thanks folks, we'll follow up in email with artifacts. bye.

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions observed ("Red wood" for Redwood, "sock two" for SOC 2), some filler words and overlapping speech.
notes: SE to validate KMS integration details and BYOK feasibility for Dedicated
Legal hold API documented and will be shared
Consider EU region provisioning for data residency during pilot
